paragraphs: Swamiji told of a sage from the age of the Upanishads who sent his son away to learn about Brahman.
When the boy returned, his father asked what he had learned. The son proudly listed the many sciences he had studied. His father was not impressed: that was nothing, he said, and sent him back.
The son went away again. When he came home, the father asked the same question and got the same kind of answer, so once more the boy was sent back.
The next time he returned, something was different. His whole face was radiant. His father rose to his feet and declared that today his son's face shone like that of one who truly knows Brahman.

Swamiji explained that when you have really known God, it shows. Your face, your voice, your whole presence changes, and you become a blessing to everyone around you. That is what it means to be a rishi, the true ideal of religion. All the talk, arguments, philosophies and even the scriptures are only preparation; the experience itself is what matters most.
learn: Knowing a lot about something is not the same as being changed by it. Let your studies and values show up in how you live, speak and treat others; that's the real proof of what you've learned.
